MY SISTER, MY BED SHARER (STAGE PLAY)
SCENE 1: HAPPY AND BUSTLING FAMILY
AT RISE: (Scene opens on a well-decorated living room.)

Mr. Ismanu and his family mime laughing and talking about random things, they are in a celebratory mood; it’s one of those days. Amidst the lightheartedness though, it can be noticed that Reverend Ismanu is paying keen attention to the mannerisms of his wife Mrs. Margaret Ismanu, and his sister Mamuna. At one point, Mamuna, sensually, butt-slaps Mrs. Margaret as she walks past her to serve her husband a glass of drink and some biscuits. Mrs. Margaret is unsure how to react, and Reverend just looks at them wryly. Mamuna momentarily attempts to break the chain of Reverend’s suspicion with a joke.
MAMUNA

Brother, your wife is endowed o; I wish I was as endowed as her. (They all laugh, except that Reverend’s laughter seems discordant and suspicious, conflicted by what he had witnessed, he excuses himself.)
REVEREND
I have some important things to take care of. (Lights flicker and go out, coming back on almost immediately to reveal the next scene.)
SCENE 2: VOICES TORMENTING THE GENDERLESS PERSON
(Dressed in black with a black mask to shield the actor’s identity; moving vigorously across the stage as if to get away from voices amidst quiet whimpers for help.)
VOICES

(Voices of every kind.)You are a horrible-terrible person! You low-life wretch! What kind of a person are you? Go find yourself a shameless being! I am ashamed to be called your mother! Woman, who is the father of that abomination?! I never knew you! I can’t leave with the fact that we are siblings! How dare you do that to the innocent girl . . . you shameless demon . . . Why introduce her into hell and not burn alone you devil?! You will never be accepted anywhere! Change your mind, change your life, and come back to your senses you despicable being! What have you done to my sister? Shame on you! What have you done to my sister? Shame on you! What have you done to my sister?!!!!!!!!!! (The last voice echoes deafeningly until the actor shouts to interrupt it and quietly the female and male voices deliver the next line while the actor  runs across the stage and into the audience  hesitantly as though imploring them, but also too scared . . . he doesn’t get dangerously close and  moves away quickly back onto the stage.)
ACTOR
(Standing center stage down, a male voice  speaks/echoes …teary, broken, and discouraged.) I just need help, love, care, and acceptance, don’t judge me...
(A female voice speaks/echoes …teary, broken, and feeling dejected.)I need your help, acceptance, love, care …  (Both voices.)…and your acceptance

(The actor falls to the floor with one knee on  the floor and face in hands and completely  covered in a show of despair, abrupt and  deafening silence follows, and lights flicker just  enough to allow the actor to exit us and allow  the next scene.)
SCENE 3: FAMILY MEETING
Trouble brewing… (The Reverend stands by the sofa, with enough light illuminating him and the sofa (not too bright though) and darkness around him.)
REVEREND

(Disdainfully but cautiously)Hello…(Pause…)  …you must come to my house today; today is the day I will prove myself and my accusations. Right beneath my roof, ah, this abomination will not continue! (He slumps into the sofa and echoes  desperation.)Mmhhm…(Sighs loudly in response, lights brighten as if to depict day break and he calls out to his daughter.
REVEREND

Shiela! Sheilaaaa!!!(Pause)Sheilaaaaaa!!(Sheila rushes into the room disheveled but it goes unnoticed.)Sheila, inform your mother to prepare to welcome our visitors  this afternoon, I am going out.(Several lights flicker once and go off abruptly, come on almost immediately to reveal an elderly man taking his seat with the other members of Reverend’s family. They all settle down, all members of the family including the two children. Then Reverend speaks…)
REVEREND

This is it…(Lights on them as they mime having an intense discussion, the elder intermittently shaking his head vigorously either in denial or acceptance. As this conversation goe on, the FIVE MINUTES SCENE will be going on with voices and everything.

SUGGESTION: This could take place on a partitioned stage or better still take place after SCENE 2.)When the FIVE MINUTES SCENE ends, that end of the stage darkens and full light and focus is placed on the EMERGENCY FAMILY MEETING as it continues with voices.)
Scene continues…
SCENE 4: FIVE MINUTES SCENE
Voices in the dark

(Both actors are dressed in black including a black mask in a dimly lit room (just enough so their movement can be seen, much left to the imagination though); a sofa in the center stage, on and around which action occurs. Sound does much to create moods ranging from yearning to agitation, to fear, then anger.)
FIRST WOMAN
I have missed you so much…
SECOND WOMAN
I am getting tired of hiding our love affair from everyone.  Sometimes I wish I could stand on the rooftop and proclaim my love to you...shout it out to all who have ears to hear.
FIRST WOMAN
(Erotic, low-pitch tone)
Yes, but first come sit with me, come rest your head on my bosom I have missed you more intensely than I can bear.
SECOND WOMAN
How I wish I had met you before, before him and now like a thief I sneak into the house that should have been mine anytime I need  rest.
FIRST WOMAN
My dear, come let's rest in each other’s arms, for the night rolls by quickly, we might lose it before we even begin.
SECOND WOMAN
Come here to me; let me kiss you passionately better than he ever has... (Passionately in each other’s arms, lips locked).
FIRST WOMAN
(Amidst moans…)This is the business I like to get down to... (Two minutes later).
FIRST WOMAN
(Softly and agitatedly)I hear movement...
SECOND WOMAN
You hear nothing love... (Both hear a subdued wimp of someone in pain and run silently and quickly into hiding, staying there for so long not knowing how many minutes had passed.)
SECOND WOMAN
(Quietly) Do you think they saw us?
FIRST WOMAN
(More agitated)I told you not to let us do it here. It’s unwise; it could have been in your bedroom.
SECOND WOMAN
(Quietly)Yes, but you should know that I want to destroy this safe haven of a lie you have and keep you all to myself. (Hearing more movement).
FIRST WOMAN
Ssshhhh, quiet… (They stay quiet for a while longer)
SECOND WOMAN
Good let's go to my room, no one saw us; come let us finish this song of love we sing each other.
FIRST WOMAN
(Irritated)No! (Quietly)I would go back to my room, lest we are caught and open up the full horrors of hell upon ourselves.
SECOND WOMAN

(Disappointed)Okay go, I will go to my room soon too. Let me remain here so we are not seen together by anyone.(First woman steps out of hiding to sneak quietly away when the second woman grabs her startling her.)
FIRST WOMAN
What now?!(Angrily but quietly)
SECOND WOMAN
I love you.
FIRST WOMAN
I love you too.(Goes away)
SCENE 5: FAMILY MEETING CONTINUES
REVEREND

MAMUNA! MAMUNA!! MAMUNA!!! How many times did I call you? Erh?  Leave my house!!! Now!!! And take with you that fellow abomination of a woman I have called my wife for all these years, never let me set eyes on the two of you again.
MRS. MARGARET
No o! Please my husband, let’s talk about this, it is all a misunderstanding… someone is trying to destroy our marriage…someone is…
REVEREND
Can you imagine the effrontery to still play the blame game when

you have been caught right in the act? I detest you, all these years, all these years… I suspected something was going on knowing well the history of this devil’s incarnate masquerading as a sibling.(More to himself)Oh! God, what sin did I commit to deserve this curse? I tried to take her into my Christian home, hoping you would purify and purge her but now she is the canker that has disintegrated my family, destroying it completely…what would people say? What would the church…my church say? The Reverend’s wife is one of them, oh, how could you? How could you? Ah, how do I answer that I have harbored someone like this in my home being a founding member of the Coalition Against LGBTQ+ Rights (CALR) in this country? You two have brought me shame unthinkable!
ELDER

Reverend calm down, that is why I am here, this is why you called me here, to talk about the matter, to understand how it started and how to end it for the continuity of the family. Think about the children, this might just be a test Reverend.
REVEREND
(Interrupts)If it is a test, then I have failed!!!! Out of my house you perverted, bed-sharing, degenerate harlots…out!
MRS. MARGARET
Honey…erm…your sister is just jealous of our union, she is trying to destroy our beautiful family, don’t let her evil plans work…
MAMUNA

Erheh? Is that so? I have been quiet all this while because I am used to these things. I have suffered being an outcast everywhere I have found myself, even from my own family. No one cares about me, society hates me, but I will not be quiet and watch you lie Missus. Who is it that wants to destroy your home; I thought you said you loved me? Coward and now…
MRS. MAGARET

Shut up! Who loves you? How can I love my fellow woman? I gave in once in a moment of weakness and you have held it over my head since, blackmailing the sanctity of my home if I ever denied you… what could I have done differently? Ah home breaker… honey, Reverend, please…
REVEREND
Don’t honey me; Jezebel from the pit of hell… is this what you want your children to emulate? Your daughter?!
SCENE 6: THE ROKI FAMILY AT THE ISMANU’S HOUSE
(Sudden terrible and angry pounding at the door of the Ismanu’s startles everyone resulting in a moment of quiet till Reverend speaks out.)
REVEREND

Who is it that wants to break my door? Come in, it is open. (Madam Rita Roki, a member of Reverend Ismanu’s church, her husband who rarely visits the church, and their only daughter Marilyn who goes to school with Sheila appear through the door. Madam Rita Roki is saddled with disbelief and distress, her husband a big time business tycoon has a murderous look on his face and their daughter Marilyn looks like her world ended yesterday. The three take in the disheveled look of the family and Mr. Roki speaks before anyone can ask him a question.)
MR. ROKI
I am here to confront that deviant who introduced my only  innocent daughter Marilyn to the devil’s ways….
REVEREND

(Obviously shocked speaks)There is no deviant or devil in my house, for your information  you are in a Reverend’s house please accord my presence and  house with some respect and explain why you are here again…
MR. ROKI

(Laughs disdainfully, deepening that angry murderous look.)  Reverend indeed! I did not come for you…(To himself)…that would be another time.(To Reverend)Once again I have come for that deviant and devil that has  ruined my daughter’s life…
REVEREND ISMANU
(More to himself.)I have one devil here, oh no two…(Looking at his wife and sister.)
MR. ROKI
(To his daughter and pointing to Sheila) Is it that the girl who introduced you? (Marilyn is hesitant)Don’t waste my time…
(He bellows angrily. This frightens Marilyn  who begins crying.)
MARILYN
(Pointing to Sheila amidst frightened tears, probably rethinking her life.)Yes, it’s that girl, Sheila…
REVEREND AND MRS. MARGARET
(Together in agitation…)What has my daughter done?
MARILYN
She initiated me at school and now I don’t like boys…
MRS. MARGARET
What is she talking about?(To no one in particular.)
REVEREND
(Overcoming his initial shock)Shut up, woman, you very well know what she is talking about…   (To Mr. Roki)Wait, how did you find out?
MR. ROKI

This lady here… (Pointing to his daughter, Marilyn)…has been inviting her female friends to the house to do group  studies. They always study…(He exaggerates study)…in her room, but as we know it, every day for the thief one  day…
REVEREND AND MRS. MARGARET
(Respond simultaneously) ...for the Master!(They both stop and look at each other;   Reverend looks at Mrs. Margaret with an   angry look and Mrs. Margaret looks quickly  away.)
MR. ROKI

My wife went upstairs to my daughter’s room after calling she  and her friend for a while without success to get them to come  down to the dining room for a snack. Unfortunately for them and  fortunately for us, her door was unlocked and what my wife saw  these two ladies doing almost made her dumb. I did not believe  my wife’s report myself until I watched the CCTV. I am going to  report your daughter to the school authorities, who knows how  many people she has corrupted…
REVEREND
Please go ahead…
MRS. MARGARET
Reverend!
REVEREND
Quiet woman! I also will report you two for whatever to be done  to you both to be done. (Calmly he asks Sheila who looks so pale it  seems she is just about to faint.)Who initiated you?
SHEILA
(She looks like she could die right there.) Auntie Muna!
MAMUNA
Herh! Shut up!
REVEREND
Why should she shut up?! Eeei, Mamuna! My daughter too?!
MRS. MARGARET
Oh you have destroyed my family, my life, my daughter’s…
REVEREND

Devil’s incarnate… I am also going to report you Mamuna for  defiling my fifteen years old daughter who is a minor in the  eyes of the law. You will rot in jail! Mark my words. (Everyone remains motionless as he speaks these words. The picture that must be achieved here is people scattered all over the sitting room and most importantly the Roki family just behind the sofa, the elders sitting uncomfortably on the sofa stage left, Sheila just by the sofa stage left, Reverend and Mamuna facing each other as they speak their final words center stage down, the others should be placed naturally or at the director’s discretion. Lights flicker twice quickly and dim as focus red  light or any other intense color is focused on Reverend and Mamuna center stage down.)
SCENE SEVEN: ALTERCATION BETWEEN REVEREND AND MAMUNA
REVEREND
You have destroyed me! You have destroyed my family! What kind  of a sister are you? I welcomed you into my house…my house! My  family…
MAMUNA

Oh so now you call me a sister? Huh? You left me to my own  devices, you forsook me when I sought shelter with you eighteen  years ago…you hurt me, you did not stand by me, you were against  me, you all were…but I expected better from a big brother and  confidante.
REVEREND
Really? You expected me to stand by you when you went about  molesting young girls?
MAMUNA
I needed help, your help, everyone’s help… I was and still am sick…I didn’t need being turned into an outcast, I needed help, understanding and just maybe acceptance.
REVEREND
Yes you were and still are sick.
MAMUNA
No, I am not, I was created this way!
REVEREND
You are sick! A canker…
MAMUNA
Yes and a canker that has destroyed your family!
REVEREND
(In disbelief.)Who are you?
MAMUNA
Your canker!
(Lights flicker and go out immediately.)
(END OF ACT)
THE WILL (AUDIO DRAMA)
SCENE 1: JEFFERSON'S HOUSE
(Water closet flushes, footsteps, a click as the light is, and the sound of brewing coffee)
(Phone rings)
Jefferson

(He answers) Hello! Yes Lawyer Ntim, (Pause) I have been busy and have been unable to visit him in the hospital. (Pause) Why do you keep repeating that I had to visit him? (Pause, sounding angrier) It is too early to have this talk Lawyer Ntim, I do not like that man and nothing you say is going to make me visit him. But (Pause) why do you keep saying that I “had” to (stresses had’) visit him, you sound like my visit to him is no longer needed. (Long Pause) He is dead? (Not sounding the least remorseful)Oh he is dead! (Sounds quite unmoved, he clears his throat). (Pause) He died last week? (Pause). . . And why am I now finding out? (Pause)  You tried calling me . . . (Pause) Oh yes, I thought you were calling to insist on me visiting him (Pause) and you called several times yesterday too (Pause) Ah yes, I was busy and could not return the calls. (Pause) His will reading is today? (Pause) Oh! (Sounds very enthusiastic). Mmm, let me check the time (Pause) it’s 8am. (Pause) I will surely be there 2 pm prompt.
SCENE 2: MR. OTI'S MANSION
(The sound of audible chattering coupled with some quiet whispers which dies down as Lawyer Ntim begins to address those present.)
Lawyer Ntim
(Shuffles some papers). Good afternoon Ladies and Gentlemen of the Oti Family.

(Varying responses of good afternoons). Thanks for making it everyone for the gathering today. And as we have all been made aware when you were informed of this meeting, we are gathered here today for the Will reading of Mr. Oti . . . we proceed with no delay. (Varying responses of ‘great’ and ‘okay’).

Now to matters. . . Mr. Oti wants you to know that he deeply cares and loves you all and hopes that the wealth he leaves you can help you establish your lives even better than it is today. (Clears his throat and pauses before he continues) Mr. Julian Oti is bequeathed the Sunrays Estate situated on 1,500 acres of land located at Trassaco Valley and 4 Regan hotels located in Awoshie, Ofankor, Nyanyanu, and Weija.

(Chattering begins undertone and ceases when the Lawyer begins speaking again). (Shuffling paper) Serwaa Oti is bequeathed the 750 acres of land located in Santase as well as the remaining 4 Regan hotels located in Lapaz, Kwashieman, Dansoman, and East Legon. That would be all . . .
Jefferson
(Butts in sharply) And what of me?!
Lawyer
Yes, Mr. Jefferson . . .(Pause). (Shuffles through his documents)
. . . I was getting there. (Pause) Mr. Oti in his will stated that you could have all he had bequeathed you only if you’d satisfy a clause.
Jefferson
(Impatiently) Wait what clause?
Lawyer Ntim
What did Mr. Oti tell you about your paternity?
Jefferson

(Impatiently)What kind of question is that, Mr. Lawyer Ntim? Do not waste my precious time, (huffs) read away the will and let me know my share of the properties that father of mine left me(rashly and harshly). (mumbles of eeiis)
Jefferson
(Claps back) What?!

(Pause then angrily) What is there to tell me about my paternity other than the fact that Mr. Oti was an irresponsible father who has thought that leaving me with my mother and providing for me financially whilst cutting me away from his immediate family was the way to be a good father? To imagine that I got to know about him only when I was in my teens, I hate him!
Julian
(Calmly but with authority) Do not talk about our father like that.
Jefferson
And what if I do? (Menacingly)
Lawyer Ntim

(Butts in)Gentlemen! There is no need for this right now. We are in mourning and we should not soil the name of the dead. (Pause) Mr. Jefferson, (Pause) Mr. Oti before his demise wanted you to know that he was not your biological father. . .
Jefferson
What?! What are you talking about? The audacity!
Julian
Yes, and we know, father told us, (short Pause) he also warned us to never let you know. He only decided to tell . . .
Jefferson
Will you shut up?!
Lawyer Ntim

Enough! (He rants out the following)Your mother was unfaithful to Mr. Oti, they divorced when he found out the truth about your paternity. He out of a kind heart, decided to continue to play a part in your upbringing financially and even promised your late mother to do so till you were of age and able to stand on your own and fend for yourself. Your mother was supposed to tell you the truth of your paternity but according to Mr. Oti she never did, it seemed. All he ever wanted to do was to support your upbringing as he once thought of you as his own. But you grew up and hated him with a passion.
Jefferson
I had every right to, and besides I don’t believe what you are claiming.
Lawyer Ntim

It doesn’t matter if you believe me or not (calmly)I am saying that, because you were unable to fulfill the clause which was to visit Mr. Oti and allow him to tell you the truth and make amends which he wanted to  so badly on his death bed, (pause)the properties which otherwise would have been yours will be sold and money donated to the poor.
Jefferson
(Screams)No! You cannot do this!
SCENE 3: JEFFERSON'S HOUSE
(All is quiet as he broods alone drinking a bottle of vodka)
Jefferson

Oh, oh, oh . . .! (Slurred speech) Oh boy! I messed up big time! I have been angry with my dad all these years thinking he didn’t love me as much as his other children but he wasn’t even my biological father.
I’ve lost it all . . . (he sobs). Nooooooooooooooooooo (screams like something out of a horror movie).
THE END
THE FOLLY OF MAN (STAGE PLAY)

A deep voice (that of the narrator, as airily as possible) seeps through the night and echoes, “And so it happened…” (followed by the crackling of thunder, and a sudden quiet, followed again by the chirping of birds and the croaking of frogs ushering in the first Act).
ACT 1: THE SHRINE (AT DAWN)

This scene opens on a shrine just before the break of dawn, poorly lit with a kerosene lantern or two, a fetish priest and an older man, they seem to be having an intense moment as the priest keeps looking into a pot and shaking his whisk over it alongside shaking his head in disbelief. The priest continues to shake his whisk over the pot anytime he looks into it as if trying to change whatever he is seeing to something else. Finally, when it seems nothing will change, he looks up to the older man and says gloomily.

Priest: The gods are tight -lipped, the picture they show is blur and they offer no explanation for the incurable ailment of your wife’s child aside letting you know that the answer you seek lies in the bosom of the child’s mother.
Opanyin: Please….

Priest: Sssshhh... listen to what the gods have to say first. The gods say that you are asleep but your legs are outside…. mmm....mm, they say that you must go and put your house in order because by a single gunshot breaking through the dawn and welcoming the first rays of the morning star the end shall be signified.

Opanyin Asem: What does all this mean Nana? Nana I am tired of parables and riddles. The gods should be fair with me, I have served them in faithfulness all these years. Please Nana plead with them on my behalf to tell me something, to at least give me the assurance that my son will live and not die.

Priest: Humph, humph… (Shaking his whisk over the pot and looking into it again) The gods say that no son coming from your loins will die because… (three gunshots are heard in quick succession startling them.
Opanyin Asem: Eeeii Nana, who could be hunting at this hour when I the greatest hunter has not yet sharpened my bows and prepared my gun for the jungle, that sounded unnatural though…

Priest: (laughs thoughtfully) Yes Opanyin, the gods speak to us all the time and in every way they can, the question to ask is, do we hear, and do we understand when we hear? Opanyin the gods have spoken (as he says this he stands up, picks his pot and whisk, turns around and retreats back into the sanctuary of the shrine leaving Opanyin seated in confusion, as he gets up to leave too the lights dim on him).
ACT 2: MARKET SQUARE (IN THE AFTERNOON)

Lights fill in on the local palm wine seller surrounded by the local palm drinkers, occupying themselves with talks of what goes on in every local’s bedroom as they sip their delicious palm wine and plunge more and more into debt with the palm wine seller, Maame Akua walks in.
Maame Akua: (to the palm wine seller) Good afternoon Auntie Esi
Auntie Esi: (looks up and on seeing Maame Akua responds disdainfully with a show of scorn) Erherh madam, to what do we owe this visit this hot afternoon, why has the bat come out of her dark place?
Man: (Clears his throat loudly) Erh Maame Palmwine, easy on the woman, she has greeted you nicely, just respond equally, if not equally just respond at least and hear her out.
Man 2: You say what? Let her accost her, Maame Palmwine go on, when she came in she saw only you to be worthy of her greetings.
Maame Akua: I am sorry o, Good afternoon.
All (except Auntie Esi): Good afternoon
Man 3: Now tell us what you came here to tell us, I am listening…
Man 1: Ah, and who said she came to talk to you, leave the poor woman alone.
Maame Akua: Actually I came to look for my brother, have you seen Awusie?
Man 3: Awusie, who is Awusie? In fact, who is your brother? You mean your husband?
Maame Akua: (looks taken aback, uncomfortable and plays with her clothes untying it to tie again)
Man 1: Will you shut up! Don’t you know her husband Opanyin Asem, the most respected hunter in this village? Have you ever seen him sit and drink with…?
Man 3: let me continue for you…low life, jobless and aimless people like us?
Man 1: Mmm. I was going to put it rather nicely but you have a point anyway…
Auntie Esi: (standing now) Oh yes, he has a point!
Man 2: Hey hey hey, Auntie Esi, don’t insult us or else we will leave your drink for you and come back for it tomorrow.

Auntie Esi: Sorry o I didn’t mean to bruise the ego that I didn’t know was there in the first place. Now let me address this woman... Maame Akua, you can leave now, as you can see Awusie is not here and your presence here is undesirable…
All: eeiiii Undesirable to who? (they all say together, look at each other’s faces and start laughing hysterically)
Auntie Esi: …to me

Man 3: Aaaaah okay, but not to us o, this woman turns heads everywhere she goes, see as she is turning my head (he looks away from Maame Akua and turns his head to look at her with his free hand slowly) and the other two men say the same and follow suit together “See the way she is turning my head” as they turn their heads to look at her again and they all laugh again.)
Maame Akua: Please if you see him…
Man 2: Oh there he is (he points to Awusie the drunk who approaches them unsteadily).

Maame Akua: Oh where is he, where is he? (She turns around and rushes to Awusie, grabs his arm and pulls him away quickly with force) Oh thank you, thank you (she says as she pulls Awusie away with her).
Auntie Esi: Look at her (she chuckles and takes and seat).
All: (Turn to look at her and continue to stare as she sits then they start talking).
Man 3: (to the others) Do you know why Auntie Esi doesn’t like Maame Akua?
Man 1: We know but tell us
Man 2: Yes, go ahead
Man 3: Opanyin Asem had eyes for her until he set his eyes on Maame Akua and he never looked back.
Man 2: Yes o Auntie Esi is jealous, she is a very jealous woman
Man 1: Yes, I told you, didn’t I?
Auntie Esi: Hey hey hey, you men will not gossip about me like I am not even here
All: Sorry o
Man 3: We will gossip like you are here
Man 2: Erherh, do you know Opanyin Asem’s son is critically ill?
Man 3: You mean Papa Awusie’s son?
Man 1: Ssshh, will you shut up? Don’t let anyone hear that from you ever again
Man 3: If it is the truth should I not say it? He is my friend I know…
Man 1: Shut up!
Man 2: Eeeeeiii eeeeeiiii ei ei ei ei ei (loudly)
Man 1: What is it?
Man 2: So it is true? I have heard the rumours, I have seen the resemblance, tell me more
Auntie Esi: Yes, tell us more (very interested now).
Man 3: So…
Man 1: Shut up! You Gossip!
Man 3: (startled but recovers quickly) ah but do you know what I want to say?
All: What?!
Man 3: Erherh, Auntie Esi wanted to marry Opanyin Asem, we must look into it, she probably has something to do with the child’s ailment.
Auntie Esi: Herh! You will be careful wai (points her finger at him threatingly) or …
Man 1: Or what?
Auntie Esi: I…
Man 2: It’s okay, it’s okay, let’s not fight. Maame Palmwine please sit down and allow us men to gossip in peace and men let us gossip like she is here okay
All: Okay
Man 2: (To Man 3) so what were you saying about Auntie Esi again?
Man 3: Erherh, so they say that Auntie Esi ….
Auntie Esi: Herh!! (Takes off her slipper and stretches her hand menacingly, the men all sway to the side to avoid the impact and they freeze.)
Lights dim out
ACT 3: OPANYIN ASEM’S HOUSE (PAST MID-NIGHT)

On the compound lies a young child, nine years old dying and covered wholly in a cloth, his head on his mother’s lap (Maame Akua) who sits on the mat too, and a man (Awusie) sprinkling some concoction on the boy from the crown of his head to the sole of his feet with some leaves as he mumbles some words only stopping once a while to catch his breath.
Maame Akua: Aha do it just like I told you, we have to do this till the break of dawn
Awusie: Eeei Maame Akua, do you want to kill me…why, won’t we sleep? I am tired o
Maame Akua: (threatingly) if you ever say that again …
Awusie: (who had knelt to rest gets up quickly and continues the incantations and sprinkling)

DA(Shocked)No! Why should I waste money on school when there are better things to use money for? If you don’t want to farm and carry firewood like every regular girl your age, go back inside. And don’t mention school again.
No school for you or any of your siblings. That money can go to better things – like the iPhone 13 Pro Max I’m saving for.
(Calls out)Children! Children!!!
(The CHILDREN come out, arranged in their tattered clothes, clearly unhappy.)
DALook, I know none of you is happy about the new “developments” in this house… but I’m trying to make you better people in this community.
(They snicker under their breath.)

DAI gave birth to nine of you so you could help me. The farm work is plenty. Now, five of you are this grown and you say you want to go to school? It won’t happen! My farm is small. I alone cannot work hard enough to feed all nine of you. If you help on the farm, we can manage.
CHILDREN(In unison)But Da…

DABut Da what?(Angry)I paid school fees for years, and what happened? You were still sacked because I said I wouldn’t pay again. Is it my fault things are hard? I went to your so-called Headmaster, wearing my kente, and explained that I have to take care of my family too. He got angry. I got angry. I didn’t pay for a term—
CHILDRENThree terms, Da.
DAErh, three terms – and so?
From now, come and help me on the farm. Besides, God blessed me with girls, and I must begin to enjoy the fruit of my labour. I’ll start marrying you off, one after the other.
CHILDRENShockedAh, Da!
DAAh, Da what? Should I not benefit from what my loins have produced? None of you five girls is a child, only Akos. And even she will be ripe in three years.
(Scanning them)Fourteen to nineteen. You are ready for marriage.
(MA enters, excited.)

MA(talking fast)Husband, I saw a beautiful expensive cloth at the market! I can’t wait to buy it and show my friends. And for the funeral, I need a new black and red cloth. I have to send it to the seamstress too—
(Stops, noticing the children)What is going on here?

DAYes, my dear, we must look very expensive at the funeral.(Laughs)I don’t even know why I’m sharpening this cutlass. I’m not going to the farm. I’m waiting for those boys to come and clear that small land for me. They’re charging a lot, but what is money compared to my rest?

AKOS(Quietly, but with courage)But Daddy, all this money you are wasting on funeral clothes and expensive phones could at least send one of us to school. If you say you cannot send all of us, maybe one…

DAWill you keep quiet? For your age, you talk about things bigger than you. I should marry you off first! I don’t want to hear “school” again. My father didn’t go to school, his father didn’t, his father’s father didn’t. What are you talking about?
JAMENA(Softly interjects)But Uncle Timo, your brother went to school.
DA(Sharp)And that is why he only has two children! Is he man enough to handle nine like me? What work do I do? Yet I live an expensive life. Don’t provoke me.
(To MA)Woman, why are you just standing there as your children talk to me like I’m their mate? Have you joined them? You haven’t even given me breakfast!
MANo o.(To the children)My friends, out of our sight! Go and set the firewood for heavy breakfast, just how your father likes it.
(The children murmur and exit to obey.)
NARRATOR(Speaking over the scene)Look at them: husband, wife, and nine children. All they think about is buying and buying and buying.

The father used to be a good farmer, until five years ago when he took a loan to expand his cocoa farm. All the money is wasted on unnecessary things. He has only this year – maybe this very month – to pay, or else the family land, used as collateral, will be taken away.
Lights fade / transition.
SCENE TWO – THE STREET
(NARRATOR steps a little forward.)
NARRATOR(To audience)Pay close attention to these ones coming. A gossip’s tongue can tell you everything happening in a whole household in just five minutes.
(GOSSIP 1, 2, 3 enter, walking as if they’re on their normal rounds.)
GOSSIP 1Did you see Akosua’s mother’s flashy dress at the market yesterday? Eei, that family, they have money o.
GOSSIP 2If they have money, why are eleven people living in one small room, with no window, not even a mosquito net?
GOSSIP 1(Laughs)Eei, my sister, how did you even know there’s no net?
GOSSIP 2I know things.
GOSSIP 1But why are their children not going to school anymore? I hear not even one of them is in school— all of them have been sacked.
GOSSIP 3My sister, say it again o. What work does the man do that he’s always buying new clothes and shoes? And have you heard?
GOSSIP 1 & 2(Leaning in)Heard what?
GOSSIP 3They say he uses an iPhone 12!
GOSSIP 2Eeeeeiii! Once upon a time he was a farmer. Now he’s just a spender!
(They all burst into laughter.)
GOSSIP 3I heard his brother in the city has only two children, but they’re in university and well cared for. Yet if you see him, he doesn’t even look rich.
GOSSIP 1Exactly! Don’t judge a book by its cover. The poor are trying to live rich while the rich live like the poor. Girls!
GOSSIP 3I also hear his daughter Jamena is pregnant.
GOSSIP 1Is that news? It was bound to happen.

GOSSIP 2Are you now hearing? Hmm. Anyway, the “rich man”—(Emphasizing)—the “rich man” whose house is collapsing is throwing a pre-birthday party for himself this evening. His birthday is next week, but he just felt like it. The music is the invitation: if you hear it…
GOSSIP 1 & 3…you attend!
GOSSIP 1Eiii… money is talking.
(They laugh. Music starts – party music. Some youngsters appear, dancing a short Shaku Shaku-style formation.)
(NARRATOR rises from her stool, steps forward.)
NARRATORThere is trouble! The bank is coming, while the cocoa farm is burning.
CHORUS(Off or on)Fire! Fire! Fire! Oh, oh, oh! Your farm is burning, Da! Your farm is burning, Da!
(All on stage panic and rush off in different directions – party cut short. Only NARRATOR remains.)
Lights shift.
SCENE THREE – THE STREET (LATER)
(GOSSIP 1, 2, 3 sneak on, looking around as if trying not to be seen.)
GOSSIP 1Did you see what happened yesterday?
GOSSIP 2Oh yes. When the Spender’s debtor came for him.
GOSSIP 3He had used his farmland and that small house as collateral. He didn’t invest the loan well, and now look.
GOSSIP 2It’s sad. A man living beyond his means, refusing to work, wasting what little he has.

GOSSIP 3They should call the rich uncle in the city. Maybe he can help.
GOSSIP 1 & 2Mmmm…
(They continue miming gossip as NARRATOR steps forward.)
NARRATORYou see, people, when a child insists on touching something red-hot, fire will teach that child a lesson.
The Spender would have been thrown out of his house if not for his brother’s intervention. He might even have ended up in jail for failing to pay his huge debt.

Let us learn to live within our means and be content with what we have. Be frugal, and use the little resources you have wisely. Wise resource management is key. And never deny your children their right to education, because human resource is the ultimate resource.
(Turns, calling)Come here, all of you!
(The whole cast – children, DA, MA, GOSSIPS, YOUNG DANCERS – run back on and gather around her.)

REWRITE THE STARS . . . (TONIGHT)
A short stage play / dance-theatre piece
CAST OF CHARACTERS

ROSALYN – A young woman, sensitive, romantic, wounded by past relationships.MICHAEL – Roselyn’s former boyfriend, affectionate but emotionally insecure.LINDEN – A sincere man, drawn to Roselyn, but limited by his own fears and boundaries.EARLIER GENTLEMAN – A memory/figure representing a previous love in Roselyn’s life (can be double-cast as MICHAEL if desired).BALLERINA – A dancer who embodies Roselyn’s inner emotional world.
SETTING
Various locations:
A stage in an auditorium (for dance sequences)
A library
A park
Linden’s living room
Time: The present.
Music: “Rewrite the Stars” from The Greatest Showman, used in sections as indicated (licensed or suitable instrumental arrangement).
SCENE 1
The Stage of an Auditorium
(Blackout. A soft golden-yellow spotlight fades up on the BALLERINA center stage. She wears a red dress.)
Music: The first male verse and chorus of “Rewrite the Stars” begins (instrumental or vocal).
(The BALLERINA dances a mimetic solo that suggests longing and reaching out toward an unseen partner. Her movement builds in intensity with the chorus, then softens as the verse ends.)
(As the music transitions out of the chorus, her movements slow. She finishes in a still, vulnerable pose. The spotlight slowly fades to black.)
Blackout.
SCENE 2
Library
(Lights rise on ROSELYN seated alone at a library table with books open in front of her. The space is quiet. A soft, neutral wash.)
ROSELYN sits staring at the books but not reading.
(Beat.)
EARLIER GENTLEMAN enters, carrying a small stack of books.
EARLIER GENTLEMAN(Softly, friendly)Need a hand?
(He takes some of her books and places them on the table. They share a brief smile.)
(Short montage can be suggested through lighting shifts and minimal movement, or done as stylized action.)
(He sits beside her, occasionally glancing at her with a warm smile.)
(He places a small gift box on the table and slides it toward her.)
(He gently takes her hands in his, holding them for a moment.)
(Beat.)
Suddenly, EARLIER GENTLEMAN is gone. The light shifts back; ROSELYN is alone at the table.
ROSELYN looks around, confused.
(Beat – confusion turns to realization.)
She lowers her head as tears fill her eyes. She takes a tissue, wipes her tears, closes her books carefully, and gathers her things.
(She stands, pauses for a moment as if listening for his presence, then exits, still dabbing her eyes.)
Lights fade.
SCENE 3
Park
(Lights up on a simple park setting: a bench, suggestion of trees. ROSELYN and MICHAEL enter, holding hands, laughing softly.)
(Brief physical sequence to show their connection: they walk, playfully bump shoulders, share a private joke.)
(Beat.)
(Images/moments can be indicated by stylized action or projections.)
MICHAEL kneels to tie ROSELYN’s loose shoelace.
He gently brushes a strand of hair from her face.
He holds her hands against his chest with both of his.
He embraces her in a warm hug.
They sit on the bench.
MICHAEL(Still a bit breathless from laughing)You know, I could do this every day.
ROSELYN(Smiling)Walk in circles and make bad jokes?
MICHAEL(Grinning)Exactly that.
(Beat. His smile fades slightly as he grows more serious.)
MICHAELRosy, I need to tell you something.
ROSELYN(Still light, trusting)Okay, love. What is it?
MICHAEL(Taking a breath, subdued)I… I don’t think I can do this anymore.
ROSELYN(Frowning)Do what?
MICHAELThis.
ROSELYN(Leans in)What is “this,” Michael?
MICHAEL(Beat, then blurts)This relationship.
(Silence.)
ROSELYN(Standing, stepping away from the bench)What are you talking about? Why?
MICHAEL(Stands slowly)I’m sorry, Roselyn. I’m scared. I don’t think I’m ready for this kind of love.(Beat.)I don’t want to keep pretending and hurt you even more later.
ROSELYN(Voice trembling)But you’re already hurting me now.
(He reaches toward her face to wipe a tear. She pulls away quickly.)
ROSELYNDon’t.
(Beat.)
MICHAEL looks at her one last time, then turns and walks away, not looking back.
ROSELYN watches him go, then her knees give a little and she sinks back onto the bench.
She begins to cry, trying to stifle the sobs but failing.

(After a moment, she pulls a book out of her bag, opens it, and reveals a photo of herself and MICHAEL. She takes the photo out, folds it into quarters with shaking hands, and places it carefully in the corner of the bench.)
(Beat.)
She wipes her face with a tissue, stands, and exits slowly, leaving the folded photo behind.
Lights fade.
SCENE 4
Linden’s Living Room
(Lights rise on a modest living room. ROSELYN sits on a sofa, arms loosely wrapped around herself. LINDEN kneels in front of her, holding a small jewelry box.)
LINDENRoselyn, please… just listen to me.
ROSELYN(Shaking her head, eyes turned away)Linden, I can’t go through this again.
LINDENI’m not asking you to jump into anything.(Beat.)Just let me be here. Let me care about you.
(He opens the jewelry box, revealing a delicate piece of jewelry, and offers it.)
ROSELYN(Looks at it, then pushes it gently back toward him)I can’t accept that. Not now. Maybe not ever.
(She starts to rise. LINDEN reaches out and lightly holds her wrist—not forceful, but desperate.)
LINDEN(Softly)Don’t run from me too.
(Beat. She looks away.)
Lights begin to fade as the moment stretches, then transition.
SCENE 5
The Stage of an Auditorium – Dance
(Spotlight up on BALLERINA, again in the red dress. The rest of the stage is dark.)
Music: Female verse of “Rewrite the Stars” beginning with “You think it’s easy…”
(BALLERINA’s movement now shows resistance and inner conflict: reaching out and pulling back, circling an invisible partner, collapsing inward and then forcing herself upright.)
(At the end of the verse, she turns away from the invisible partner, wrapping her arms around herself. The light fades.)
Blackout.
SCENE 6
Linden’s Living Room
(Lights up on the same living room. ROSELYN sits on the sofa, LINDEN now on a chair nearby, leaning slightly forward.)

LINDENI love you, Roselyn.(Beat.)I’m not like the others who stepped in and out of your life. I love you, and I will keep loving you if you let me.(Leans in)Let me love you tonight… and tomorrow… and the day after that.
(Beat.)

ROSELYN(Softly, eyes fixed on her hands)I don’t know if I can believe that.(Beat.)My heart’s been broken so many times it feels beyond repair. Love always seems to end in rejection and loneliness. I’ve learned to suffer in silence.
(She looks up, meeting his gaze.)
ROSELYNThis thing… this thing called love never seems to last. They all said to me, “Let me love you tonight.”(Beat.)But like a candle in the wind, the flame always went out.
LINDENThis time can be different.(Leans forward more)This love can last. Just give me a chance, Roselyn. Let me love you genuinely, starting tonight.
(Beat. ROSELYN holds his gaze for a long moment, then a shy smile trembles onto her lips. She looks away, torn.)
Lights dim slowly, transitioning to the next scene.
SCENE 7
The Stage of an Auditorium – Duet Section
(Spotlight on BALLERINA. The stage remains otherwise dark.)
Music: Duet section of “Rewrite the Stars.”

(BALLERINA dances as though with an unseen partner: turns, near-lifts, almost-embraces. Her choreography mixes hope with hesitation. She reaches for something that almost—but never quite—settles into place.)
(At the end of the duet, she spins away and freezes in a fragile, open pose, as if waiting to see if someone will catch her.)
Lights fade.
SCENE 8
Linden’s Living Room / Various Locations (Montage)
(A flexible staging: the montage can be suggested via lighting changes and minimal set pieces.)
(Lights: warm afternoon – ROSELYN and LINDEN share ice cream, laughing; a drip of ice cream falls, they laugh harder.)
(Lights shift to evening – they walk under streetlights, close together.)
(Lights shift to night – they sit side by side on a rooftop or balcony, fingers intertwined, looking at the stars.)
(Lights shift to early morning – they share a simple breakfast. ROSELYN looks genuinely relaxed and happy.)
(The montage ends with a clear look at ROSELYN’s renewed trust.)
Lights settle back into LINDEN’s living room.
ROSELYN(Jumps up joyfully)Linden, let’s go see my parents.(Beat, excited)I want them to meet you.
(LINDEN’s smile fades just slightly. He hesitates.)
LINDEN(Shakes his head slowly)Roselyn… I don’t think that’s a good idea.
ROSELYN(Playful at first, lightly tugging his hand)Come on, don’t be shy. They’re going to love you.
(She pulls him toward the open door. She steps through the doorway. He stops at the threshold.)
(Beat.)
ROSELYN turns back. LINDEN remains in the doorway, unmoving.
ROSELYN(Confusion shifting into fear)Linden…?
LINDEN(Quietly, almost apologetic)I didn’t lie to you.(Beat.)I did love you. I still do. But I never promised more than tonight, did I?
(Silence.)
ROSELYN stands outside, suddenly alone in the light. LINDEN stays framed in the doorway, a clear line between them.
(Beat.)
The light around LINDEN slowly fades until only ROSELYN is lit.
ROSELYN’s shoulders sink. She turns away from the doorway and walks off, slowly, the joy drained from her steps.
Lights fade to black.
SCENE 9
The Stage of an Auditorium – Final Dance
(A single spotlight rises slowly on the BALLERINA center stage. Her movements are slower now, weighted with sorrow.)
Music: Final female verse and closing lines of “Rewrite the Stars.”
(She dances with smaller, more contained gestures—reaching toward the audience, then toward the empty space where a partner should stand, but nobody appears. Each reach falls back into herself.)
(As the music reaches its emotional peak, she begins a controlled, slow fall to the floor, one arm reaching up as if trying to hold onto a fading light.)
(She settles on the ground, the last note lingering. She mouths—or softly whispers—the word:)
BALLERINA(Almost inaudible)Tonight.
(The spotlight tightens to a small circle around her face or outstretched hand, then fades to black.)
End of Play.
